newsitem.title: GERMANY: German recovery gaining strength - Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: German recovery gaining strength - Rexrodt.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday that third quarter output data showed the country's economic recovery was gaining in strength.
Preliminary data released earlier showed that gross domestic product (GDP) had risen by one percent in the third quarter compared with the second quarter, and by 2.4 percent year-on-year.
"Recovery forces are gaining strength," Rexrodt said in a statement. "We can look with optimism to next year."
Rexrodt said that the latest data confirmed official growth forecasts. The government expects GDP to grow by 1.25 percent this year and by 2.5 percent in 1997.
He also said that improved investment was helping to broaden the basis of recovery, which has so far been driven by exports.
Conditions for extending the recovery -- including low interest rates, pay settlements and price stability -- were in place, Rexrodt said.

"There are good prospects for turning the current recovery into a sustained economic upswing," he said. But, he added, hopes for easing high unemployment would only come from sustained recovery and strong investment.
